mainTopic: Is a lender holding collateral a שומר שכר or a שומר חנם, and what is the root of the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא?
overview: The גמרא is trying to explain why our משנה calls a lender holding collateral (משכון) a שומר שכר, while רבי אליעזר in a ברייתא treats him as a שומר חנם. The first two attempts to make them agree fail. The first runs into the wording of the משנה. The second, a split between lending money and lending produce, runs into רבי יהודה's clause and would push the משנה away from רבי עקיבא. So the גמרא concludes that the משנה simply does not follow רבי אליעזר. It then asks what רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא really argue about. Its first guess is שמואל's rule of the sickle handle, but that is rejected, since everyone disagrees with שמואל when the משכון is cheap. Its second guess is רבי יצחק's rule that a lender acquires the משכון, but that rule may apply only to a משכון taken after the loan. Its third guess ties the argument to the dispute of רבה and רב יוסף about someone guarding a lost item. When the גמרא asks whether this makes רב יוסף's view an argument between תנאים, it answers no, and starts a new explanation that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Both sources use the same wording
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא knocks down the earlier answer, which had split the cases by when the collateral was taken. Our משנה says 'he lent him on collateral,' which means the collateral came with the loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: But our משנה says 'he lent him on collateral'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is attacking the earlier attempt to make the משנה and רבי אליעזר's ברייתא agree. That attempt said one case took the collateral at the time of the loan and the other took it later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answer put our משנה in a case where the collateral was taken after the loan, which is why the lender would be a שומר שכר. But the משנה's phrase 'הלוהו על המשכון' means the collateral was part of the loan from the start. So the משנה cannot be about collateral taken later, and the old distinction collapses.

keyTerms.meaning: he lent him
collateral, an item held as security for a loan
it teaches / the text says

phrases.english: It teaches 'he lent him on collateral'!
phrases.notes: These are the words of our משנה. They mean the collateral was handed over right when the loan was made.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the previous answer, which split the cases by when the collateral was taken.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier distinction: collateral taken at the time of the loan versus collateral taken afterward.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says 'הלוהו על המשכון', which means the collateral was given at the time of the loan. So the משנה cannot be about collateral taken afterward.

steps.title: A new split: lending money versus lending produce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a different answer. The ברייתא is talking about a loan of money, and the משנה is talking about a loan of produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, there is no difficulty. Here the case is where he lent him money; there the case is where he lent him produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up the old answer and tries a new way to make the two sources fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When someone lends produce, he gains something, because he gets fresh produce back instead of produce that would spoil. Since he benefits, he is a שומר שכר on the collateral, which fits the משנה. When someone lends money he gains nothing, so he is only a שומר חנם, which fits רבי אליעזר's ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult
here... there (each source is about a different case)
money
produce

phrases.english: Rather, it is not difficult:
here, where he lent him money,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the ברייתא of רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: there, where he lent him produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that step 1 knocked down.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): the two sources are about different kinds of loans.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא seemed to disagree about the very same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a money loan (שומר חנם), and the משנה is about a produce loan (שומר שכר).

steps.title: רבי יהודה's clause shows the first opinion makes no such split
steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה brings רבי יהודה, who is the one who splits money from produce. That implies the first opinion in the משנה does not split them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the end of the משנה teaches that רבי יהודה says, 'If he lent money, he is a שומר חנם; if he lent produce, he is a שומר שכר,' we can infer that the תנא קמא makes no difference between them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the money-versus-produce answer by pointing to the last part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the money/produce split is presented as רבי יהודה's own view, then the first, anonymous opinion must disagree with it. So the תנא קמא holds that every lender on collateral is a שומר שכר, even a lender of money. That still conflicts with רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: the latter clause of the משנה
an unpaid guardian, with lighter liability
a paid guardian, with heavier liability
by inference / it follows that
the first, anonymous opinion in the משנה

phrases.english: But from the fact that the latter clause teaches,
Rabbi Yehuda says:
if he lent him money, he is an unpaid guardian,
if he lent him produce, he is a paid guardian.

phrases.aramaic: מִכְלָל דִּלְתַנָּא קַמָּא לָא שָׁנֵי לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: By inference, for the first Tanna there is no difference!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the money/produce split offered in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה's first opinion is only about produce loans.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the split belonged to the תנא קמא as well, רבי יהודה would have no reason to state it as his own view. So the תנא קמא must make no split.

steps.title: The whole משנה is רבי יהודה, with words missing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the entire משנה follows רבי יהודה. The משנה is missing some words, and once we fill them in, it already contains the money/produce split.
steps.simpleTranslation: The whole משנה is רבי יהודה, and words are missing. This is what it teaches: one who lent on collateral is a שומר שכר. When is this said? When he lent produce. But if he lent money, he is a שומר חנם. As רבי יהודה says: if he lent money, he is a שומר חנם; if he lent produce, he is a שומר שכר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rescues the money/produce answer. It does this by reading the משנה as one opinion, רבי יהודה's, with a missing clause filled in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there is no separate תנא קמא who disagrees with רבי יהודה. The first line, 'שומר שכר', is only about produce loans, and money loans are a שומר חנם. So the משנה no longer clashes with רבי אליעזר about money loans.

keyTerms.meaning: all of it, the whole משנה
it is missing words (the text is incomplete)
and this is what it teaches
in what case is this said?

steps.confusionAlert: With חסורי מחסרא, the גמרא is not saying the משנה is wrong. It means the משנה is written briefly, and we must read in words that were left out.

phrases.english: The whole of it is Rabbi Yehuda,
and it is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
one who lent him on collateral is a paid guardian;
in what case is this said? Where he lent him produce,
but if he lent him money, he is an unpaid guardian.
For Rabbi Yehuda says:
if he lent him money, he is an unpaid guardian,
if he lent him produce, he is a paid guardian.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלַּהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא, וְחַסּוֹרֵי מִיחַסְּרָא וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי יהודה's clause in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: חסורי מחסרא: reading the משנה as incomplete and filling in the missing words.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה has a תנא קמא who makes no split, against רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole משנה is רבי יהודה. A lender of produce is a שומר שכר, and a lender of money is a שומר חנם.

steps.title: Then the משנה goes against רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: If the whole משנה follows רבי יהודה, then for money loans it rules 'שומר חנם'. That puts the משנה against רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the משנה ends up not following רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out an unwanted result of the last answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds that a lender on collateral bears the loss like a שומר שכר, even for a money loan. Reading the משנה as רבי יהודה means the משנה rejects רבי עקיבא's view. The גמרא is not willing to accept that.

keyTerms.meaning: if so
it ends up standing as / it turns out

phrases.english: If so,

phrases.aramaic: קָמָה לַהּ מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.english: our Mishna ends up not according to Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, קָמָה לַהּ מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the cost of the answer in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the whole משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading makes a money lender a שומר חנם, which goes against רבי עקיבא. The anonymous משנה should not be pushed away from רבי עקיבא's view.

steps.title: Final conclusion: the משנה does not follow רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא stops trying to make the משנה and רבי אליעזר agree. It concludes plainly that the משנה follows the view that disagrees with רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear: our משנה does not follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: After all the attempts fail, the גמרא returns to its original simple statement and settles on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the efforts to fit the משנה with רבי אליעזר either clashed with the wording or pushed the משנה away from רבי עקיבא. So the simplest answer stands. The משנה says a lender on collateral is a שומר שכר, which agrees with רבי עקיבא and disagrees with רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: it is clear (the final, settled answer)

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה (a lender on collateral is a שומר שכר) does not follow רבי אליעזר. Every attempt to fit them together failed.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear:
our Mishna is not according to Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מְחַוַּורְתָּא מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Drops the reconciliation attempts after the problem raised in step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה follows the view that a lender on collateral is a שומר שכר. It disagrees with רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: Maybe they argue about שמואל's rule of the sickle handle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא argue about a cheap משכון, and the question is whether we follow שמואל's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say they argue where the משכון is worth less than the loan, and the question is שמואל's rule. שמואל said: if someone lent his friend a thousand זוזים and the borrower left a sickle handle as a משכון, then if the handle is lost, all thousand זוזים are lost.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first guess about the root of the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא. It ties the argument to a rule of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל holds that losing the משכון cancels the whole loan, even when the משכון is worth very little. The suggestion is that רבי עקיבא (the money is lost) agrees with שמואל, and רבי אליעזר (the lender swears and collects his money) does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say: the גמרא is offering a suggestion
Collateral, an item the borrower leaves with the lender
The amount of the money (the size of the loan)
The handle of a sickle, a cheap item
They argue

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא בִּדְלָא שָׁוֵי מַשְׁכּוֹן שִׁיעוּר זוּזֵי,
phrases.english: Let us say: where the collateral is not worth the amount of the money,
and they argue about the rule of שמואל.
phrases.notes: 'They' are רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא, who argue about a lost משכון.

phrases.english: As שמואל said:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי מַאן דְּאוֹזְפֵיהּ אַלְפָּא זוּזֵי לְחַבְרֵיהּ
phrases.english: Someone who lent a thousand zuz to his friend
and the borrower placed with him a sickle handle for them,
phrases.notes: 'For them' means as collateral for the thousand zuz.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבַד קַתָּא דְמַגְּלָא – אֲבַדוּ אַלְפָּא זוּזֵי.
phrases.english: if the sickle handle is lost, the thousand zuz are lost.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא בִּדְלָא שָׁוֵי מַשְׁכּוֹן שִׁיעוּר זוּזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the משנה has been tied to one side, the גמרא asks what the two sides actually argue about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suggestion: רבי עקיבא holds like שמואל that losing even a cheap משכון cancels the whole loan, and רבי אליעזר does not.

steps.title: No one holds like שמואל when the משכון is cheap
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. When the משכון is worth less than the loan, everyone disagrees with שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the case is where the משכון is worth less than the loan, then everyone disagrees with שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the first suggestion. Neither רבי אליעזר nor רבי עקיבא would agree with שמואל in that case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both תנאים reject שמואל's rule, that rule cannot be what they argue about. So their argument must be about a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone, meaning both sides of the argument
They do not hold of it

phrases.aramaic: אִי בִּדְלָא שָׁוֵי מַשְׁכּוֹן שִׁיעוּר זוּזֵי –
phrases.english: If it is where the collateral is not worth the amount of the money,
then everyone does not hold of שמואל's rule,

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בִּדְלָא שָׁוֵי מַשְׁכּוֹן שִׁיעוּר זוּזֵי – דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לֵית לְהוּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion made in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the argument is about שמואל's rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both sides reject שמואל's rule when the משכון is worth less than the loan, so it cannot be their point of argument.

steps.title: Instead, maybe they argue about רבי יצחק's rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves the argument to a case where the משכון is worth the full loan. It suggests they argue about רבי יצחק's rule that a lender acquires the משכון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is where the משכון is worth the full loan, and they argue about רבי יצחק's rule. רבי יצחק said: How do we know that a lender acquires the משכון? Because the פסוק says, 'and it shall be צדקה for you.' If he did not own the משכון, what צדקה would there be in returning it? From here we learn that a lender acquires the משכון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second explanation for the argument. It brings רבי יצחק's proof from a פסוק that the lender becomes a kind of owner of the משכון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Returning the משכון at night is called צדקה. That only makes sense if the lender is giving up something that belongs to him. The suggestion is that רבי עקיבא accepts רבי יצחק's rule: the lender owns the משכון, so he bears its loss and his loan is wiped out. רבי אליעזר does not accept the rule, so the lender only swears and collects.

keyTerms.meaning: A lender (creditor)
Acquires the collateral, becomes a kind of owner of it
Righteousness, a good deed
From where do we know?

phrases.english: But here it is where the collateral is worth the amount of the money,
and they argue about the rule of רבי יצחק.
As רבי יצחק said:
From where do we know that a lender acquires the collateral?
As it says: "And it shall be righteousness for you."
phrases.notes: דברים 24:13. The פסוק is about returning a poor man's משכון at sunset.

phrases.english: If he does not acquire the collateral,
from where does he get righteousness?
phrases.notes: Giving back something that isn't yours is no special good deed.

phrases.english: From here we learn that a lender acquires the collateral.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכָא בִּדְשָׁוֵי שִׁיעוּר זוּזֵי, וְקָא מִיפַּלְגִי בִּדְרַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting שמואל's rule, the גמרא offers a different root for the argument.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the argument to a different case and a different underlying rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument is about שמואל's rule for a cheap משכון.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is about a משכון worth the full loan, and whether the lender acquires it as רבי יצחק says.

steps.title: רבי יצחק may only mean a משכון taken after the loan
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the second suggestion. רבי יצחק may have said his rule only about a משכון taken after the loan, not one given when the loan was made.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you really think so? You can say רבי יצחק meant a case where the lender took the משכון after the loan was made. But where he took it at the time of the loan, did רבי יצחק say his rule?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that רבי יצחק's rule fits our case. It splits between a משכון taken later and one given at the time of the loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case of רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא is a loan given with a משכון from the start. If רבי יצחק's rule covers only a משכון taken later, it does not apply here. Then it cannot explain their argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you really think so? (the גמרא pushing back)
He took a משכון from him
At the time of the loan
Did he say? (meaning: he did not say)

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not reject רבי יצחק's rule itself. It only questions whether that rule reaches a משכון given at the time of the loan.

phrases.english: And do you really think so?
You can say that רבי יצחק said his rule
where he took the collateral not at the time of the loan,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מִשְׁכְּנוֹ בִּשְׁעַת הַלְוָאָתוֹ – מִי אָמַר?
phrases.english: but where he took the collateral at the time of the loan, did he say it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִסְבְּרָא? אֵימוֹר דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בְּמִשְׁכְּנוֹ שֶׁלֹּא בִּשְׁעַת הַלְוָאָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the suggestion from step 9 by limiting רבי יצחק's rule.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Questions whether רבי יצחק's rule applies to a loan given with a משכון from the start.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יצחק may have spoken only about a משכון taken after the loan, while our case is a משכון given when the loan was made.

steps.title: A third suggestion: they argue about a finder who guards a lost item
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that everyone agrees with רבי יצחק when the משכון was taken after the loan. So it places the argument on a משכון given when the loan was made. It suggests the תנאים argue about the rule of a שומר אבידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when he took the משכון not at the time of the loan, everyone holds like רבי יצחק. Here the case is a משכון taken at the time of the loan, and they argue about one who guards a lost item.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the point from Step 10 and offers a new explanation of the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא. It ties their argument to the law of someone guarding a lost item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 showed that רבי יצחק's rule may only apply to a משכון taken after the loan. So the גמרא now says: in that case nobody argues, and the real case is a משכון given when the loan was made. In that case the lender does not acquire the משכון, so the גמרא needs a different reason why רבי עקיבא would treat him as a paid guard, and it compares him to a finder guarding a lost item.

keyTerms.meaning: At the time of his loan, meaning the משכון was given when the money was lent
Not at the time of his loan, meaning the משכון was taken later
Everyone; all the opinions agree
Someone who found a lost item and is guarding it until the owner comes
They argue about

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of משכון. Here the גמרא agrees that nobody argues about a משכון taken after the loan. The argument is only about a משכון given when the loan was made.

phrases.english: Rather, his collateral taken not at the time of his loan –

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק.
phrases.english: everyone holds like רבי יצחק.
phrases.notes: He means רבי יצחק's rule that the lender acquires the משכון, which is what Step 10 was about.

phrases.english: And here it is about collateral taken at the time of his loan,
and they argue about one who guards a lost item.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the limitation raised in Step 10 and offers a new explanation of the argument.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the argument to a different underlying principle (the law of a שומר אבידה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנאים argue about רבי יצחק's rule that a lender acquires the משכון.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees with רבי יצחק about a משכון taken later. For a משכון given at the time of the loan, they argue about the law of a שומר אבידה.

steps.title: The source: רבה and רב יוסף argue about a finder's responsibility
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the אמוראים dispute it is relying on. רבה says a finder guarding a lost item is like an unpaid guard. רב יוסף says he is like a paid guard.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was said: about one who guards a lost item, רבה said he is like an unpaid guard, and רב יוסף said he is like a paid guard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its new suggestion by quoting a known argument between רבה and רב יוסף. Now we can see which תנא matches which אמורא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומר חנם is only liable if he was careless, while a שומר שכר is also liable if the item is stolen or lost. The idea is that a lender holding a משכון is like a finder holding a lost item. So רבי אליעזר, who calls the lender an unpaid guard, matches רבה, and רבי עקיבא, who calls him a paid guard, matches רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: Unpaid guard, liable only if he was careless
Paid guard, also liable if the item is stolen or lost

steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute about a שומר אבידה is now the key to the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא. The rest of the passage tests whether this link really works.

phrases.english: As it was stated: one who guards a lost item,
רבה said: he is like an unpaid guard;
רב יוסף said: he is like a paid guard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the dispute of the אמוראים that Step 11 relies on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה: a שומר אבידה is like a שומר חנם. רב יוסף: a שומר אבידה is like a שומר שכר.

steps.title: Does this mean רב יוסף's view is disputed by a תנא?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי אליעזר matches רבה, then רבי אליעזר seems to disagree with רב יוסף. The גמרא asks whether רב יוסף's view is really a matter of argument between תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב יוסף's view is a dispute between תנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks what follows from its new suggestion. If it is true, then רב יוסף's rule is not accepted by everyone, because רבי אליעזר would disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא's view is weaker if a תנא openly disagrees with it. The גמרא wants to know if this suggestion forces רב יוסף into that weak spot, or if his rule can fit both תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? Opens a suggestion that is often rejected
תנאים; the view depends on an argument between Sages of the משנה period

phrases.english: Shall we say that the view of רב יוסף is a dispute between תנאים?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out a troubling result of the suggestion in Steps 11-12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the new suggestion means רבי אליעזר disagrees with רב יוסף, or whether רב יוסף's rule can fit both תנאים.

steps.title: No: everyone may agree with רב יוסף about a lost item
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers no. About a finder guarding a lost item, everyone, even רבי אליעזר, agrees with רב יוסף. It then starts to explain what the case here is really about.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. About one who guards a lost item, everyone holds like רב יוסף. And here...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea that רבי אליעזר disagrees with רב יוסף. The words 'and here' set up the next move, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא says the lost-item case is agreed by everyone, so the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא must come from something else about the lender. The גמרא explains that difference on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: No; rejecting the suggestion just made
They hold; they accept the view of
And here; introduces how to understand the case at hand

phrases.english: No,

phrases.aramaic: בְּשׁוֹמֵר אֲבֵידָה – דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף,
phrases.english: regarding one who guards a lost item, everyone holds like רב יוסף,
and here,
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next amud, where the גמרא explains what the argument is really about.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, בְּשׁוֹמֵר אֲבֵידָה דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13 by denying that רבי אליעזר disagrees with רב יוסף.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Everyone, including רבי אליעזר, agrees with רב יוסף about a שומר אבידה. The argument must rest on something else, which the גמרא starts to explain with 'and here'.
